newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Strong currency worries Guatemala - Arzu.
newsitem.headline: Strong currency worries Guatemala - Arzu.

text.p: Guatemala is more concerned with the strength of its currency rather than its weakness, President Alvaro Arzu said Friday.
"Our concern is the revaluation of our currency because that influences our exports," Arzu said during a news conference.
He said Guatemala's concern was the opposite of other unspecified countries in Latin America where exchange rates are considered too weak.
"We were very worried last week because the exchange rate of the Guatemalan quetzal against the dollar (strengthened) from 6.03 to 5.98," the president said.

Friday's bank rate for the quetzal versus the dollar was 5.98898/6.00616. The quetzal has strengthened steadily throughout 1996, trading at approximately 6.14 to the dollar at the beginning of the year.
